signal: Factory and goods activity is running hot (ISM manufacturing 55.5, production at a 5-year high) while Q3 GDP was revised up to 4.3%.

evidence.fact: ISM manufacturing PMI 55.5 in Oct vs 54.5 in Sep; production index 59.0, highest since Nov 2021; supplier deliveries 59.1 (slower)
Q3 real GDP +4.3% annualized, revised up from 3.4%
Transportation and warehousing +25k jobs in Oct, +104k since Feb

so_what: Freight-linked businesses get volume from strong goods output; hot supplier-delivery times mean tight capacity, which supports pricing.
ask_next: Do carload, intermodal and truck volumes and pricing confirm the ISM strength, or is it inventory build ahead of price rises?

signal: Fed is set to keep raising rates into a weak housing sector; minutes say mortgage activity fell and housing is weak.

evidence.fact: Minutes: residential mortgage activity declined further amid the sharp rise in mortgage rates; housing and other interest-sensitive sectors weak
Almost all participants see further hikes as appropriate; Dec 8-9 meeting; SEP median 2026 funds rate 4.1 vs 3.875 midpoint now
10y Treasury 4.85% on 2026-11-25, down from 5.15% on Nov 13 but above 4.31% in April

so_what: Builders and mortgage lenders face high borrowing costs for buyers; a late-November drop in long yields is the first relief.
ask_next: How much of the Nov 18-25 fall in 10-year yield feeds into mortgage rates, and do builder orders and incentives show it?

signal: Bank shares fell sharply in the Oct meeting window on slower loan growth and commercial real estate worries, while risky-credit spreads widened.

evidence.fact: Bank equity prices fell sharply on slower loan growth and CRE exposures; speculative-grade spreads widened, data-centre financed high-yield worst
Lending standards in the Oct Senior Loan Officer survey were slightly easier than historical medians; card delinquencies elevated

so_what: Credit stress looks selective (AI-linked borrowers, leveraged software, CRE), not broad. Banks with CRE or card exposure are the squeezed ones; diversified lenders less so.
ask_next: Which large banks show CRE, card and data-centre lending exposure in their latest 10-Q, and are reserves building?

signal: PCE inflation (3.3% core) now runs well above CPI (core 2.6%), and the Fed ties price pressure to AI-buildout demand for tech goods.

evidence.fact: Core PCE +3.3% y/y, headline 3.8% y/y in Oct
Minutes: many participants say AI-buildout demand strains supply and raises tech goods prices; unusual CPI-PCE discrepancy

so_what: Suppliers of AI hardware have pricing power while buildout continues; Fed says a slowdown in AI spending would ease inflation, a risk for the same suppliers.
ask_next: Do chip and equipment makers show rising average selling prices and backlog, and how exposed are they to a funding pullback?

signal: Energy remains the loudest CPI item: gasoline +37% y/y, fuel oil +74% y/y (Sep), and ISM prices indexes above 70.

evidence.fact: Gasoline +37.4% y/y in Oct; energy +0.7% m/m after +5.2% in Sep
Minutes: refined fuel supply constraints; diesel costs straining agriculture

so_what: Fuel buyers pay far more; whether they pass it on decides who is squeezed. Producers and refiners gain.
ask_next: Which airlines and truckers show fuel cost pass-through (fares, surcharges) versus margin loss in their latest filings?

signal: Nominal spending is inflated by fuel prices while real consumer spending stalled in October.

evidence.fact: Retail sales +6.8% y/y nominal; gas stations +30.3% y/y; ex-gas only +0.1% m/m
Real PCE about 0.0% in Oct; saving rate 4.1%

so_what: Card networks earn on nominal dollars, so inflation lifts volumes even if real spending is flat; household budgets for necessities are under strain.
ask_next: Do network and processor volume growth figures in the latest filings track nominal sales, and is the mix shifting to debit or low-ticket?

signal: Long yields are falling while the Fed leans toward a December hike: market and Fed disagree.

evidence.fact: 2y 4.80% to 4.61%, 10y 5.07% to 4.85% from Nov 18 to Nov 25; 3m bill 4.34% above funds ceiling 4.00%
Minutes: a couple of participants would consider more than 25bp if inflation data are unfavorable

so_what: If the yield drop holds, rate-sensitive, debt-heavy groups get relief; if the Fed hikes anyway it reverses.
ask_next: What changed on Nov 19-20 to move yields (check Fed speeches, Treasury, EIA)? Does it persist after the Dec 4 jobs report?
